Anti-Ragging:
Anti-Ragging Policy

Zero Tolerance Towards Ragging

At MAM School of Engineering, we are committed to providing a safe, respectful, inclusive, and student-friendly learning environment where every student can pursue academic excellence with dignity and confidence. The institution follows a Zero Tolerance Policy towards Ragging and strictly complies with the provisions of the University Grants Commission (UGC) Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions, 2009, the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) Anti-Ragging Regulations, the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Ragging Act, 1997, and all subsequent guidelines issued by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, UGC, AICTE, Anna University, and the Government of Tamil Nadu.

The College firmly believes that every student has the right to study in an environment free from fear, intimidation, harassment, humiliation, discrimination, or any form of physical or psychological abuse. Ragging, in any form, is strictly prohibited within the campus, hostels, transportation facilities, sports grounds, cafeterias, and any location connected with the institution.

What is Ragging?

As defined under the UGC Regulations, 2009, ragging includes any act by one or more students that causes or is likely to cause physical or psychological harm, embarrassment, harassment, fear, shame, or intimidation to another student, particularly freshers. Ragging may be committed individually or collectively and includes direct, indirect, verbal, physical, psychological, or online misconduct.

Ragging includes, but is not limited to:

  • Physical assault or abuse.
  • Verbal abuse, insults, or offensive language.
  • Mental harassment, humiliation, or intimidation.
  • Forcing students to perform embarrassing or degrading acts.
  • Compelling students to obey unreasonable commands.
  • Restricting the freedom of movement of students.
  • Social isolation or exclusion.
  • Bullying, stalking, or threatening behaviour.
  • Damage to personal belongings.
  • Online or cyber ragging through social media, messaging platforms, emails, or other digital media.
  • Any act affecting the dignity, self-respect, physical well-being, or mental health of another student.

Even an act performed "for fun" or "as an introduction" may amount to ragging if it causes discomfort, fear, humiliation, or harassment

Legal Framework

The institution strictly follows the following statutory provisions:

  • University Grants Commission (UGC) Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions, 2009.
  • AICTE Regulations for Prevention and Prohibition of Ragging in Technical Institutions.
  • Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Ragging Act, 1997.
  • Directions issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India for prevention and elimination of ragging.
  • Guidelines issued by the Ministry of Education, Government of India.

Under these regulations, ragging is treated as a serious misconduct as well as, where applicable, a criminal offence.

Objectives of the Anti-Ragging Policy

The institution aims to:

  • Create a safe and welcoming environment for every student.
  • Protect the dignity and rights of all students.
  • Prevent every form of ragging within and outside the campus.
  • Promote mutual respect, discipline, and ethical behaviour.
  • Encourage healthy interaction between senior and junior students.
  • Ensure prompt reporting and immediate action against any incident.
  • Provide counselling and support to affected students.
  • Create awareness regarding the legal consequences of ragging.

Anti-Ragging Squad

The College constitutes an Anti-Ragging Committee in accordance with UGC and AICTE regulations. The Committee is headed by the Principal.

Preventive Measures

To ensure a ragging-free campus, the institution undertakes several preventive initiatives, including:

  • Orientation programmes for newly admitted students.
  • Awareness sessions on anti-ragging laws and student responsibilities.
  • Separate interaction programmes for freshers and senior students.
  • Display of anti-ragging posters and warning notices across the campus.
  • Continuous monitoring of hostels and common areas.
  • Faculty mentoring and student counselling.
  • CCTV surveillance at strategic locations.
  • Regular meetings of Anti-Ragging Committee and Squad.
  • Anonymous complaint reporting mechanism.
  • Close coordination with hostel wardens and student mentors.

Students and parents are also informed about the institution's anti-ragging policy during admission.

Student Responsibilities

Every student shall:

  • Treat fellow students with dignity and respect.
  • Maintain discipline and ethical conduct.
  • Refrain from participating in or encouraging ragging.
  • Immediately report any incident of ragging.
  • Cooperate during inquiries.
  • Respect institutional rules and regulations.

Silence or failure to report ragging may also be viewed seriously if it amounts to aiding or concealing misconduct.

Parent Responsibilities

Parents and guardians are expected to:

  • Educate their wards about the harmful effects and legal consequences of ragging.
  • Encourage them to maintain discipline and respect fellow students.
  • Cooperate with the institution in promoting a safe campus environment.
  • Submit the mandatory Anti-Ragging Undertaking during admission wherever applicable.

Punishment for Ragging

Any student found guilty of ragging shall face disciplinary action as prescribed under UGC Regulations, AICTE guidelines, and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Ragging Act. Depending on the severity of the offence, one or more of the following actions may be taken:

  • Warning or written apology.
  • Suspension from classes.
  • Debarring from examinations.
  • Cancellation of scholarships or fellowships.
  • Suspension from hostel.
  • Withholding of academic results.
  • Debarring from placement and campus recruitment.
  • Rustication from the institution.
  • Expulsion from the institution.
  • Cancellation of admission.
  • Filing of a police complaint and initiation of criminal proceedings wherever required.

The institution reserves the right to impose appropriate disciplinary measures after following due process in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Reporting Ragging

Students are encouraged to report incidents of ragging immediately to:

  • Principal
  • Anti-Ragging Committee
  • Anti-Ragging Squad
  • Head of the Department
  • Faculty Mentor
  • Hostel Warden
  • Student Counsellor

Every complaint will be treated confidentially, investigated promptly, and appropriate action will be taken without delay.

Students may also report incidents through the National Anti-Ragging Helpline and the online anti-ragging portal established under the UGC Regulations.

Our Commitment

MJM School of Engineering is dedicated to fostering a campus culture based on respect, equality, inclusiveness, compassion, and professionalism. We believe that every student deserves a secure environment that promotes learning, innovation, and personal growth without fear or intimidation. Every member of the institution—students, faculty, staff, parents, and visitors—shares the responsibility of ensuring that our campus remains completely free from ragging.

Together, let us build a campus where respect replaces fear, friendship replaces intimidation, and learning thrives in a safe and supportive environment.

Grievance Redressal:
Student Grievance Redressal Cell

Fair, Transparent and Time-Bound Grievance Redressal Mechanism

At MAM School of Engineering, we are committed to providing a fair, transparent, inclusive, and student-centric academic environment where every student is treated with dignity, equality, and respect. The institution has established a Student Grievance Redressal Cell (SGRC) to ensure that students' grievances are addressed promptly, impartially, and confidentially.

The Grievance Redressal Cell functions in accordance with the University Grants Commission (Redressal of Grievances of Students) Regulations, 2023, the guidelines of the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), Anna University, the Government of Tamil Nadu, and other statutory regulatory authorities governing higher education. The institution believes that an effective grievance redressal mechanism strengthens transparency, accountability, student satisfaction, and institutional governance.

Objectives

The Student Grievance Redressal Cell has been established with the following objectives:

  • To provide students with a fair and accessible mechanism for resolving grievances.
  • To ensure timely and transparent disposal of complaints.
  • To promote justice, equality, and accountability within the institution.
  • To safeguard the rights and interests of students.
  • To create a positive academic environment free from discrimination and unfair practices.
  • To encourage students to voice genuine concerns without fear of retaliation.
  • To continuously improve institutional policies and services through constructive feedback.

Scope of Grievances

Students may submit grievances relating to any academic or administrative matter, including but not limited to:

Academic Matters

  • Teaching and learning issues
  • Internal assessment and evaluation
  • Attendance-related grievances
  • Laboratory facilities
  • Examination-related issues
  • Academic regulations
  • Project supervision
  • Availability of learning resources

Administrative Matters

  • Admission process
  • Fee-related issues
  • Scholarships
  • Certificates and transcripts
  • Identity cards
  • Hostel administration
  • Transport facilities
  • Library services
  • Internet and IT services

Student Welfare

  • Student amenities
  • Campus infrastructure
  • Drinking water and sanitation
  • Cafeteria facilities
  • Sports and recreation
  • Placement support
  • Mentoring and counselling
  • Accessibility for differently abled students

Other Matters

  • Unfair treatment
  • Discrimination
  • Delay in administrative services
  • Any deficiency in institutional services affecting students

The Student Grievance Redressal Cell does not ordinarily deal with matters that fall under specialized statutory committees, such as:

  • Ragging (Anti-Ragging Committee)
  • Sexual harassment (Internal Committee under the POSH Act)
  • Examination malpractice
  • Disciplinary proceedings already under inquiry

Such matters shall be referred to the appropriate statutory committee in accordance with applicable regulations.

Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC)

The College constitutes a Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) as prescribed under the UGC Regulations.

The Committee generally consists of:

  • Principal – Chairperson
  • Senior Faculty Members
  • Heads of Departments
  • Faculty Representatives
  • Student Welfare Officer
  • Student Representatives (where applicable)
  • Special Invitees, whenever necessary

The Committee functions independently and follows the principles of natural justice, ensuring that every complainant receives a fair hearing before any decision is made.

Guiding Principles

The grievance redressal mechanism is based on the following principles:

  • Fairness
  • Transparency
  • Confidentiality
  • Impartiality
  • Accountability
  • Timely disposal
  • Equal opportunity
  • Respect for natural justice

Every complaint is handled objectively without bias or discrimination.

Grievance Redressal Procedure

The institution follows a structured and time-bound grievance redressal process.

Step 1: Submission of Grievance

Students may submit their grievances through:

  • Online Grievance Portal
  • Email
  • Written application
  • Department Office
  • Principal's Office
  • Student Welfare Office
  • Suggestion/Complaint Box (where available)

The complaint should clearly mention:

  • Student Name
  • Register Number
  • Department and Year
  • Contact Details
  • Nature of Grievance
  • Supporting Documents (if any)

Step 2: Acknowledgement

Every grievance received is acknowledged and recorded.

Step 3: Preliminary Review

The Committee examines whether the grievance falls within its jurisdiction.

If necessary, additional information may be sought from the student or concerned department.

Step 4: Hearing

Both the complainant and the concerned parties are given an opportunity to present their views.

The Committee follows the principles of fairness and natural justice.

Step 5: Resolution

After careful examination, the Committee recommends suitable corrective measures to the competent authority.

Wherever possible, grievances are resolved within the timelines prescribed under the applicable regulations.

Confidentiality

The institution maintains strict confidentiality throughout the grievance redressal process.

  • Identity of the complainant is protected wherever appropriate.
  • Records are maintained securely.
  • Information is disclosed only to authorized officials involved in the inquiry.
  • Students shall not face retaliation for filing genuine grievances.

Rights of Students

Every student has the right to:

  • Submit a grievance without fear.
  • Be treated with dignity and respect.
  • Receive a fair and unbiased hearing.
  • Know the status of the grievance.
  • Receive a reasoned decision.
  • Appeal, wherever permitted under applicable regulations.

Responsibilities of Students

Students are expected to:

  • Submit truthful and complete information.
  • Maintain respectful communication.
  • Cooperate during the inquiry.
  • Avoid frivolous or malicious complaints.
  • Follow institutional rules and regulations.

Knowingly submitting false or malicious complaints may invite appropriate disciplinary action.

Online Grievance Redressal

In line with the UGC Regulations, the institution provides an online mechanism for submitting and monitoring grievances. Students can submit complaints electronically, upload supporting documents, and receive updates regarding the status of their grievance. The College continually reviews and strengthens its grievance redressal mechanism to ensure greater transparency and accessibility.

Appeal Mechanism

If a student is dissatisfied with the decision of the Student Grievance Redressal Committee, the grievance may be pursued further in accordance with the provisions of the UGC (Redressal of Grievances of Students) Regulations, 2023, including the appellate mechanism before the Ombudsperson appointed by the University, wherever applicable.

Our Commitment

MAM School of Engineering is committed to creating a campus culture founded on fairness, transparency, integrity, and mutual respect. We believe that an effective grievance redressal mechanism not only resolves individual concerns but also contributes to continuous institutional improvement. Every student is encouraged to communicate genuine concerns without hesitation, knowing that they will be heard, respected, and addressed in a professional and timely manner.

By maintaining an efficient grievance redressal system, the institution reaffirms its commitment to student welfare, quality education, and good governance.
